newsitem.title: UK: Petrol spills into Channel after ships collide.
newsitem.headline: Petrol spills into Channel after ships collide.

text.p: Two tankers collided in the Channel on Saturday and shipping sources said about 9,500 tonnes of petrol had spilled into the sea.

The Norwegian-owned M/V Bona Fulmar, carrying a consignment of unleaded petrol, and the Mexican chemical tanker Teoatl crashed in thick fog about 30 miles from the English port of Dover. Both ships were afloat and the crews were safe.

Norway's Bona Shipping said the incident was under control and divers were on their way to seal the damaged hull of the 78,600-tonne Bona Fulmar which is at anchor. When the ship is safe it will proceed to the Dutch port of Rotterdam for repairs.
"It's a big spillage but it's lucky it's petrol which will evaporate," a spokesman at Lloyd's shipping intelligence service said on Sunday.
The 21,650-tonne Mexican chemical tanker was on its way to the Dutch port of Rotterdam for repairs.
There were no more further details.
